sources.name: Draft scores written by Claude from general botanical knowledge (unverified)

families.name: Asteraceae
families.tip: What looks like one flower is a head of many tiny florets, often with strap-shaped rays round the edge and a ring of green bracts beneath. Dandelions, thistles, daisies, ragworts.

families.name: Rosaceae
families.tip: Usually 5 separate petals, many stamens and leafy stipules at the base of the leaf stalk; fruits often fleshy (hips, haws, brambles, cherries).

families.name: Poaceae
families.tip: Round, usually hollow stems with solid joints; long narrow leaves with a sheath wrapping the stem and a small flap (ligule) where blade meets sheath. Flowers in tiny green spikelets.

families.name: Fabaceae
families.tip: Pea-flowers: a large upper petal, two side wings and a boat-shaped keel. Leaves usually compound, often with tendrils; fruit a pod.

families.name: Cyperaceae
families.tip: Grass-like, but stems usually solid and triangular ('sedges have edges'); leaves in three ranks with no ligule flap. Cotton-grasses and spike-rushes belong here too.

families.name: Brassicaceae
families.tip: Four petals in a cross, six stamens (four long, two short); fruit a pod that splits from the bottom, leaving a papery central wall. Often a cress-like taste.

families.name: Caryophyllaceae
families.tip: Leaves in opposite pairs on stems swollen at the joints; five petals, often notched or deeply split (stitchworts, campions, chickweeds).

families.name: Apiaceae
families.tip: Tiny flowers in umbrella-shaped clusters (umbels), usually white; leaves often finely divided with a sheathing base; stems often hollow and ridged. Some are very poisonous.

families.name: Lamiaceae
families.tip: Square stems, opposite leaves, two-lipped flowers in rings up the stem; many smell when crushed (mints, dead-nettles, thymes).

families.name: Plantaginaceae
families.tip: A mixed family: plantains (ribbed leaves, brown flower spikes), speedwells (4 blue petals, 2 stamens), foxglove, toadflaxes, water-starworts.

families.name: Ranunculaceae
families.tip: Many stamens and separate petals or petal-like sepals; leaves often deeply lobed; fruit a cluster of small dry seeds. Buttercups, anemones, columbines, Clematis.

families.name: Orchidaceae
families.tip: Six petal-like parts, the lowest forming a distinctive lip, often patterned or spurred; leaves with parallel veins, sometimes spotted.

families.name: Polygonaceae
families.tip: A papery sheath (ochrea) round the stem above each leaf base; small flowers, 3 to 6 parts; fruit a 3-sided nut. Docks, sorrels, knotweeds, bistorts.

families.name: Amaranthaceae
families.tip: Small green flowers in dense clusters; leaves often mealy or fleshy; plants of bare and salty ground (goosefoots, oraches, glassworts).

families.name: Boraginaceae
families.tip: Rough, bristly hairs; flowers in coiled sprays that unroll as they open, often turning from pink to blue (forget-me-nots, comfreys, borage).

families.name: Amaryllidaceae
families.tip: Six-petalled flowers from a papery sheath; leaves strap-like from a bulb. Onions and garlics (umbels, onion smell), daffodils (with a trumpet), snowdrops.

families.name: Orobanchaceae
families.tip: Semi-parasites (eyebright, yellow-rattle, cow-wheat, lousewort) with two-lipped flowers; broomrapes have no green at all.

families.name: Ericaceae
families.tip: Small evergreen shrubs with bell- or urn-shaped flowers; leaves often tiny, needle-like or leathery (heathers, bilberry, rhododendron).

families.name: Juncaceae
families.tip: Grass-like; rushes have round stems, often filled with white pith; woodrushes have flat, hairy-edged leaves. Flowers small, brown, six-parted.

families.name: Iridaceae
families.tip: Sword-shaped leaves in a flat fan; showy flowers with 6 parts and 3 stamens (irises, crocuses, montbretia).

families.name: Asparagaceae
families.tip: Bulb or rhizome plants with parallel-veined leaves and six-parted flowers: bluebell, lily-of-the-valley, Solomon's-seal, butcher's-broom.

families.name: Geraniaceae
families.tip: Five separate petals and a long beak-like fruit (the 'crane's bill'); leaves usually lobed like a hand or finely divided.

families.name: Campanulaceae
families.tip: Bell-shaped, usually blue flowers; milky sap; ovary below the flower (harebell, bellflowers, sheep's-bit).

families.name: Primulaceae
families.tip: Five petals joined at the base, with the stamens opposite the petal lobes (primroses, cowslips, loosestrifes, scarlet pimpernel).

families.name: Crassulaceae
families.tip: Thick, fleshy, water-storing leaves; star-shaped flowers. Walls, rocks and dry places (stonecrops, houseleek, navelwort).

families.name: Caprifoliaceae
families.tip: Opposite leaves; includes honeysuckle, teasels and scabiouses (flower heads), valerians and snowberry.

families.name: Aspleniaceae
families.tip: Ferns: no flowers; fronds uncurl from a crozier and carry spore patches underneath. Spleenworts, lady-fern, hard-fern, bladder-ferns.

families.name: Papaveraceae
families.tip: Poppies: 4 crumpled petals, many stamens, often milky or coloured sap. Fumitories and corydalis have small tubular, spurred flowers.

families.name: Saxifragaceae
families.tip: Small plants of rocks, mountains and damp places; five petals, often white; leaves frequently in a basal rosette. Golden-saxifrages have no petals.

families.name: Potamogetonaceae
families.tip: Water plants with floating or submerged leaves and small green flower spikes held above the water.

families.name: Onagraceae
families.tip: Four petals and a long, thin ovary below the flower; seeds often with silky hairs (willowherbs, evening-primroses, enchanter's-nightshade has 2 petals).

families.name: Salicaceae
families.tip: Trees and shrubs with catkins, male and female on separate plants; seeds with cottony hairs.

families.name: Rubiaceae
families.tip: Leaves in whorls (rings) of 4 to 12 round square stems; tiny 4-petalled flowers. Cleavers is the sticky one.

families.name: Polypodiaceae
families.tip: Ferns: no flowers. Buckler-ferns, male-fern, shield-ferns and polypodies, with round spore patches on the frond underside.

families.name: Hypericaceae
families.tip: Opposite leaves, often with see-through dots when held up to the light; yellow flowers with many stamens in bundles.

families.name: Euphorbiaceae
families.tip: Spurges have milky sap and odd cup-like green flower clusters with no petals; dog's mercury has small green flowers on spikes.

families.name: Plumbaginaceae
families.tip: Coastal plants with leaves in a basal rosette; pink or lavender flowers with papery calyces (thrift heads, sea-lavender sprays).

families.name: Gentianaceae
families.tip: Hairless plants with opposite leaves and petals joined into a tube with 4 to 5 spreading lobes (centauries, gentians, yellow-wort).

families.name: Scrophulariaceae
families.tip: Figworts have square stems and small brown two-lipped flowers; mulleins have tall spikes of yellow flowers and often woolly leaves. Buddleja belongs here.

families.name: Araceae
families.tip: Lords-and-ladies: a hooded leaf-like spathe round a club-shaped spike, then red berries. Duckweeds (tiny floating green discs) are in this family too.

families.name: Oxalidaceae
families.tip: Clover-like leaves of three heart-shaped leaflets that fold down at night; five petals; sharp-tasting.

families.name: Solanaceae
families.tip: Five petals joined into a star or bell, with stamens forming a cone in the centre; fruit a berry or capsule. Many poisonous (bittersweet, deadly nightshade, henbane).

families.name: Violaceae
families.tip: Five unequal petals, the lowest with a backward spur; leaves often heart-shaped (violets and pansies).

families.name: Aizoaceae
families.tip: Introduced succulents with thick, three-sided or cylindrical leaves and large daisy-like flowers with many narrow petals; coastal cliffs.

families.name: Malvaceae
families.tip: Mallows: five notched petals and a central column of stamens; fruit like a round cheese. Limes are trees with a strap-like bract on the flower stalk.

families.name: Hydrocharitaceae
families.tip: Water plants: frogbit (floating, kidney-shaped leaves, 3 white petals), water-soldier, and the submerged waterweeds with whorled leaves.

families.name: Alismataceae
families.tip: Wetland plants with long-stalked basal leaves and flowers with 3 white or pale pink petals (water-plantains, arrowhead).

families.name: Araliaceae
families.tip: Ivy: evergreen climber with lobed leaves on climbing stems and ball-shaped umbels of greenish flowers in autumn. Marsh pennywort has round, umbrella-like leaves.

families.name: Lentibulariaceae
families.tip: Insect-catching plants: butterworts have sticky, pale green leaf rosettes; bladderworts float in water with tiny bladder traps.

families.name: Betulaceae
families.tip: Trees and shrubs with catkins in late winter or spring; fruits are nuts (hazel), tiny winged seeds (birch) or woody 'cones' (alder).

families.name: Pinaceae
families.tip: Conifers with needles (single, in pairs or in bunches) and woody cones (pines, spruces, firs, larch).

families.name: Liliaceae
families.tip: Bulb plants with large six-petalled flowers and parallel-veined leaves (fritillary, tulips, lilies, yellow star-of-Bethlehem).

families.name: Equisetaceae
families.tip: No flowers; jointed, ridged stems with rings of tiny teeth and whorls of thin green branches; spores in a cone at the stem tip.

families.name: Viburnaceae
families.tip: Shrubs with opposite leaves and flat-topped clusters of small white flowers, then berries (elder, guelder-rose, wayfaring-tree). Moschatel is a small herb.

families.name: Asphodelaceae
families.tip: Mostly introduced: New Zealand flax (huge leathery sword leaves), red-hot pokers, day-lilies; six-parted flowers.

families.name: Typhaceae
families.tip: Tall water-edge plants with long flat leaves: bulrushes have brown sausage-shaped heads; bur-reeds have spiky green balls.

families.name: Convolvulaceae
families.tip: Twining climbers with funnel-shaped flowers and arrow-shaped leaves. Dodders are leafless pink threads with no green.

families.name: Fagaceae
families.tip: Trees with catkins; fruit a nut in a cup or husk (acorns, beech-mast, sweet chestnuts).

families.name: Oleaceae
families.tip: Opposite leaves; flowers with 4 joined petals and 2 stamens, or no petals in ash. Ash has winged 'keys'; privet has black berries.

families.name: Sapindaceae
families.tip: Trees with opposite leaves: maples and sycamore have lobed leaves and paired winged fruits; horse-chestnut has hand-like compound leaves and conkers.

families.name: Urticaceae
families.tip: Small green flowers in dangling tassels; stinging nettle has stinging hairs, pellitory-of-the-wall does not.

families.name: Lycopodiaceae
families.tip: No flowers; creeping or upright stems densely covered in small, narrow, overlapping leaves; spores in cones or leaf bases.

families.name: Grossulariaceae
families.tip: Shrubs with lobed, maple-like leaves and hanging sprays of small flowers, then berries (currants, gooseberry, which is spiny).

families.name: Cistaceae
families.tip: Low, often woody-based plants of dry grassland with crumpled, short-lived yellow petals and many stamens.

families.name: Haloragaceae
families.tip: Submerged water plants with feathery leaves in whorls; small flowers on spikes above the water.

families.name: Linaceae
families.tip: Slender plants with narrow, untoothed leaves and 5 separate petals that drop quickly (fairy flax is white, flax blue).

families.name: Cornaceae
families.tip: Opposite leaves whose veins curve round towards the tip; 4-petalled flowers in flat clusters; dogwood has red winter stems.

families.name: Ulmaceae
families.tip: Trees with rough, toothed leaves that are lopsided at the base; fruit a flat papery wing round a seed.

families.name: Ophioglossaceae
families.tip: Small ferns with a single leaf and a separate spore-bearing spike or branch.

families.name: Cupressaceae
families.tip: Conifers with tiny scale-like or short prickly leaves; juniper has blue-black berry-like cones.

families.name: Aristolochiaceae
families.tip: Introduced woodland plants with heart- or kidney-shaped leaves and odd tubular or cup-shaped brownish flowers.

families.name: Montiaceae
families.tip: Small, fleshy, hairless plants with 5 white or pink petals; spring-beauty has a leaf collar round the stem below the flowers.

families.name: Resedaceae
families.tip: Spikes of small yellowish flowers with deeply cut petals and many stamens (weld, wild mignonette); bare chalky ground.

families.name: Pteridaceae
families.tip: Ferns: no flowers. Maidenhair fern has black stalks and fan-shaped leaflets; parsley fern grows in upland screes.

families.name: Nymphaeaceae
families.tip: Large round floating leaves with a slit to the centre; big white or yellow flowers floating or held just above the water.

families.name: Berberidaceae
families.tip: Spiny shrubs with yellow flowers and berries; Oregon-grape has holly-like compound leaves.

families.name: Vitaceae
families.tip: Woody climbers with tendrils; Virginia-creeper has hand-like leaves that turn red; small greenish flowers, then berries.

families.name: Polygalaceae
families.tip: Small plants of grassland and heath with blue, pink or white flowers: two large petal-like side sepals and a fringed lower petal.

families.name: Balsaminaceae
families.tip: Succulent stems; hooded, spurred flowers; seed pods that explode when touched (Himalayan balsam, touch-me-not).

families.name: Acanthaceae
families.tip: Introduced: large glossy, deeply lobed leaves and tall spikes of hooded flowers under spiny purple bracts.

families.name: Droseraceae
families.tip: Small bog plants with rosettes of round or narrow leaves covered in sticky red hairs that trap insects.

families.name: Isoetaceae
families.tip: No flowers; underwater rosettes of stiff, quill-like leaves at the bottom of clear lakes; spores at the leaf bases.

families.name: Lythraceae
families.tip: Purple-loosestrife: tall spikes of magenta flowers with 6 crinkled petals by water. Water-purslane is small and creeping.

families.name: Apocynaceae
families.tip: Trailing evergreen periwinkles with glossy opposite leaves and blue flowers whose 5 petals look twisted like a propeller.

families.name: Anacardiaceae
families.tip: Introduced stag's-horn sumach: shrub with velvety shoots, long pinnate leaves that turn red, dense red fruit clusters.

families.name: Phrymaceae
families.tip: Waterside plants with opposite leaves and large yellow, two-lipped, snapdragon-like flowers, often red-spotted.

families.name: Rutaceae
families.tip: Introduced aromatic shrubs with gland-dotted leaves (Mexican orange-blossom, rue).

families.name: Rhamnaceae
families.tip: Shrubs with small greenish 4 to 5-parted flowers and black berries; buckthorn is thorny with opposite leaves, alder buckthorn is thornless.

families.name: Hymenophyllaceae
families.tip: Tiny ferns with translucent fronds one cell thick, on wet shaded rocks and tree trunks in the west.

families.name: Celastraceae
families.tip: Spindle: shrub with green stems and pink four-lobed fruits with orange seeds. Grass-of-Parnassus: white 5-petalled flowers with fringed glands, wet places.

families.name: Juglandaceae
families.tip: Introduced trees with large aromatic pinnate leaves and catkins; walnuts, wing-nuts.

families.name: Acoraceae
families.tip: Iris-like leaves that smell of tangerines when crushed; a green finger-like flower spike sticking out sideways from a leaf-like stem.

families.name: Menyanthaceae
families.tip: Water plants: bogbean has three-part leaves and fringed white-pink flowers; fringed water-lily has small round floating leaves and yellow flowers.

families.name: Dennstaedtiaceae
families.tip: Fern: no flowers. Bracken has tall, single, much-divided fronds rising from underground stems, often in large stands.

families.name: Thymelaeaceae
families.tip: Shrubs with leathery leaves crowded towards the shoot tips and scented four-lobed flowers, then poisonous berries (mezereon, spurge-laurel).

families.name: Santalaceae
families.tip: Mistletoe: evergreen ball of forked green stems in trees, white berries. Bastard-toadflax: small parasitic herb of chalk grassland.

families.name: Zosteraceae
families.tip: Marine plants: long, grass-like ribbon leaves on sandy and muddy shores below the tide line.

families.name: Myricaceae
families.tip: Low shrub of bogs with grey-green leaves that smell resinous when crushed; catkins in spring.

families.name: Elatinaceae
families.tip: Tiny creeping plants of lake edges and mud with opposite leaves and minute pinkish flowers.

families.name: Ceratophyllaceae
families.tip: Rootless submerged water plants with whorls of stiff, forked, finely toothed leaves.

families.name: Cannabaceae
families.tip: Hop: twining rough-stemmed climber with lobed leaves and papery, cone-like female flower heads.

families.name: Juncaginaceae
families.tip: Grass-like plants of salt marsh and wet ground with fleshy, narrow leaves and a long slender spike of tiny green flowers.

families.name: Elaeagnaceae
families.tip: Spiny shrub with narrow silvery leaves and bright orange berries, mostly on sand dunes.

families.name: Selaginellaceae
families.tip: Small moss-like plant with tiny pointed leaves, in wet upland grassland and flushes; no flowers.

families.name: Pittosporaceae
families.tip: Introduced evergreen shrubs or trees with glossy leaves and small dark purple scented flowers; south-west coasts.

families.name: Ruppiaceae
families.tip: Submerged plants of brackish pools with thread-like leaves; flowers on long stalks.

families.name: Myrtaceae
families.tip: Introduced evergreen shrubs with aromatic, gland-dotted opposite leaves, white flowers with many stamens and edible berries.

families.name: Nothofagaceae
families.tip: Introduced trees planted for forestry, similar to beech but with smaller leaves.

families.name: Verbenaceae
families.tip: Wiry plant with square stems, lobed opposite leaves and long thin spikes of tiny lilac flowers.

families.name: Sarraceniaceae
families.tip: Introduced to a few bogs: leaves form upright tubes (pitchers) that trap insects.

families.name: Aquifoliaceae
families.tip: Evergreen tree or shrub with glossy, usually spiny leaves, small white 4-petalled flowers and red berries.

families.name: Alstroemeriaceae
families.tip: Garden escape with twisted leaf stalks and showy streaked flowers with 6 tepals.

families.name: Melanthiaceae
families.tip: Woodland plant with a single ring of four broad leaves and one starry green flower, then a black berry.

families.name: Marsileaceae
families.tip: Tiny fern of pond margins with grass-like leaves that uncurl like a crozier and pea-sized spore pills at the base.

families.name: Limnanthaceae
families.tip: Garden escape (poached-egg plant): white petals with yellow centres and divided leaves.

families.name: Lauraceae
families.tip: Bay: evergreen tree or shrub with aromatic leathery leaves used in cooking.

families.name: Frankeniaceae
families.tip: Low, mat-forming plant of salt marshes with tiny inrolled leaves and small pink flowers.

families.name: Eriocaulaceae
families.tip: Western Scottish and Irish lakes: underwater rosettes of grass-like leaves and small white button-heads on leafless stalks above the water.

families.name: Gunneraceae
families.tip: Introduced: gigantic rhubarb-like leaves on prickly stalks, with a huge cone-like spike of tiny flowers.

families.name: Butomaceae
families.tip: Tall water-edge plant with three-angled leaves and an umbel of pink six-petalled flowers.

families.name: Cabombaceae
families.tip: Introduced aquarium plant: submerged fan-shaped, finely divided opposite leaves and small white flowers.

families.name: Buxaceae
families.tip: Evergreen shrub with small, glossy, oval opposite leaves and tiny greenish flowers; chalk slopes and gardens.

families.name: Calceolariaceae
families.tip: Introduced: pouched, slipper-shaped yellow two-lipped flowers.

families.name: Colchicaceae
families.tip: Pink crocus-like flowers in autumn without leaves; broad leaves appear in spring. Poisonous.

families.name: Cucurbitaceae
families.tip: Climber with coiled tendrils, rough lobed leaves, greenish-white flowers and red berries.

families.name: Diapensiaceae
families.tip: Very rare: cushion plant on one Scottish mountain, with white five-petalled flowers.

families.name: Dioscoreaceae
families.tip: Twining climber with glossy heart-shaped leaves, small greenish flowers and red berries; no tendrils.

families.name: Pontederiaceae
families.tip: Introduced water plants with glossy leaves and spikes of blue flowers.

families.name: Portulacaceae
families.tip: Fleshy, sprawling annual with small yellow flowers; a garden weed.

families.name: Polemoniaceae
families.tip: Ladder-like pinnate leaves and clusters of blue bell-shaped flowers; limestone in northern England.

families.name: Paulowniaceae
families.tip: Introduced tree with very large, soft, opposite leaves and upright clusters of violet foxglove-like flowers.

families.name: Phytolaccaceae
families.tip: Introduced tall plant with reddish stems, upright spikes of small flowers and dark purple berries.

families.name: Moraceae
families.tip: Introduced tree with heart-shaped, sometimes lobed leaves, milky sap and blackberry-like fruits.

families.name: Osmundaceae
families.tip: Large fern of wet places whose fertile fronds end in rusty-brown, flower-like spore clusters; no true flowers.

families.name: Paeoniaceae
families.tip: Garden escape with large red flowers and divided leaves.

families.name: Nartheciaceae
families.tip: Bog plant with flat, sword-shaped leaves and spikes of starry orange-yellow flowers.

families.name: Scheuchzeriaceae
families.tip: Very rare bog plant with grass-like leaves that have a pore at the tip, and a few yellowish-green flowers.

families.name: Salviniaceae
families.tip: Introduced tiny floating fern forming red or green carpets on still water; no flowers.

families.name: Saururaceae
families.tip: Introduced: heart-shaped leaves smelling of orange peel and spikes of tiny flowers with four white petal-like bracts.

families.name: Tropaeolaceae
families.tip: Garden escape with round, umbrella-like leaves and orange or yellow spurred flowers.

families.name: Tofieldiaceae
families.tip: Small northern plant of wet flushes with a fan of short flat leaves and a tight head of pale greenish-white flowers.

families.name: Simaroubaceae
families.tip: Introduced tree with very long pinnate leaves, unpleasant-smelling when crushed, and twisted winged fruits.

families.name: Cyatheaceae
families.tip: Introduced tree-fern (Dicksonia) with a fibrous trunk topped by large fronds; south-west gardens and woods.

families.name: Taxaceae
families.tip: Evergreen conifer with flat, dark green needles in two rows and red fleshy cups around single seeds; no cones. All parts except the red flesh are poisonous.

species.name: Lamium album
species.tip: Looks like a stinging nettle but has white flowers and does not sting.

species.name: Lamium purpureum
species.tip: Upper leaves crowded and tinged purple; an annual of gardens and bare ground.

species.name: Lamium amplexicaule
species.tip: Upper leaves have no stalk and clasp the stem in pairs beneath the flowers.

species.name: Lamium galeobdolon
species.tip: Yellow flowers with reddish streaks on the lower lip; an ancient-woodland indicator.

species.name: Glechoma hederacea
species.tip: Kidney-shaped, round-toothed leaves on long creeping stems; smells pungent when crushed.

species.name: Prunella vulgaris
species.tip: Dense, squarish flower head with purple-tinged bracts and a pair of leaves just below it. Common in lawns.

species.name: Stachys sylvatica
species.tip: Dark wine-red flowers with white markings; stinks when crushed.

species.name: Stachys palustris
species.tip: Paler pinkish-purple flowers than Hedge Woundwort; narrow leaves with little or no stalk.

species.name: Mentha aquatica
species.tip: Rounded lilac flower head at the stem tip; strong mint smell.

species.name: Mentha arvensis
species.tip: Flowers only in whorls up the stem; the stem ends in leaves, not flowers.

species.name: Thymus drucei
species.tip: Low mats of tiny leaves; stems hairy on two opposite sides only.

species.name: Origanum vulgare
species.tip: Loose, branched clusters with purple bracts; smells of oregano.

species.name: Teucrium scorodonia
species.tip: Pale greenish-yellow flowers with no upper lip; wrinkled, sage-like leaves; acid soils.

species.name: Ajuga reptans
species.tip: Glossy leaves, leafy runners and a very short upper lip.

species.name: Galeopsis tetrahit
species.tip: Bristly stem that swells just below each pair of leaves.

species.name: Ballota nigra
species.tip: Rank-smelling hedgerow plant; the calyx has broad, spreading teeth.

species.name: Clinopodium vulgare
species.tip: Flower whorls wrapped in long, bristly hairs, so they look woolly; only faintly aromatic.

species.name: Lycopus europaeus
species.tip: Deeply toothed to lobed leaves; tiny purple-dotted white flowers in tight whorls.

species.name: Scutellaria galericulata
species.tip: Flowers in pairs in the leaf axils, all facing one way; calyx has a small hump.

species.name: Betonica officinalis
species.tip: Rosette of long-stalked, oblong leaves; reddish-purple flowers in a dense spike.
